sourceImage: references/eiffel-hero.png (user-supplied reference image; not redistributed in this repository)

referenceCamera.note: Measurer verdict (evidence/reference/measurements.json camera): perspective, near-orthographic long lens, level camera (measured pitch estimate 1.38 deg, roll 0.01 deg; level_camera_confirmed false, so pitch is authored 0 and the estimate is documented). Yaw=0 is well determined by the symmetry axis at x=543.5 px (0.5005 of frame). Measured framing: silhouette bbox x 172..915 px, y 24..1395 px -> tower height 94.68% of the 1448 px frame and body height 1371 px; camera height 0.51 * 330 = 168.3 m (horizon model). Focal length is NOT identifiable from one symmetric view (measurer range 12-25 deg vertical); 18 deg at ~1100 m is the authoring estimate that frames 330 m at 94.7%. solved=false until an overlay review confirms the exact framing.

objectClass.primaryType: architectural iron lattice tower (Eiffel Tower scale model)
objectClass.notes: Pale ivory/silver painted iron lattice tower on a near-white seamless studio backdrop, front elevation. Four splayed legs on stepped stone plinths joined by a decorative arch band, three platform bands, a glazed ribboned cupola and a thin antenna with a star finial.

reasoning: Silhouette is a stepped taper interrupted by three platform bands, four splayed legs and an arch band: high silhouette complexity (3/3).
43 named parts are visible or inferable from the reference; hierarchy is depth-3 (macro/meso/micro) with repeated systems at every level (3/3).
Lattice panels, chord rows, rivets, balusters and frieze arches are all repeated systems: repetition density 3/3, and they dominate recognisability.
Four reference-derived material responses plus a utility backdrop; local detail density includes rosettes, muntins, rivet catch-lights and paint wear (3/3 local detail).
Single view: rear legs/plinth depth are symmetry-inferred, so occlusion risk is moderate (2/3), not high.
Detachable legs/platform stack/cupola/antenna pivots are wanted for review and future actions (2/3).

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex architectural subject: the identity lives in repeated lattice/chord/rivet systems and in the three platform steps, so the spec needs macro/meso/micro levels, at least one repetition system and material local overrides, not a single blockout mass.

detailInventory.note: Every identity-defining mark was scanned zone by zone (apex, cupola, platform 3, upper shaft, platform 2, mid shaft, platform 1, arch band, legs, plinths, material response). Each detail maps to a real component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry; none is prose-only.

details.description: 12-point star finial: thin radial points on a small hub at the mast tip.
Stacked rings/crossarms around the antenna base, ~4 rings over 4 m.
12 radial ribs over the ribbed dome, reading as dark seams under the key light.
Arched glazing mullions on the lantern drum: 3 arches per visible face.
Baluster row around the platform-3 disc; ~28 visible balusters.
X-lattice panels in the upper shaft: 26 chord rows x 4 faces, diagonals ~60 deg.
Rivet bands along every horizontal chord: rows of small domes at ~0.55 m pitch.
Modillion row under the platform-2 deck: closely spaced console blocks.
Platform-1 frieze arcade: continuous row of small arches under the deck.
Platform-1 railing balusters: the densest repeated verticals on the model.
Console brackets under platform-1 deck: paired curved braces per bay.
Rosette medallions (small raised discs) along the arch band intrados.
Four concentric arch ribs forming the decorative band between the legs.
details.zone: base arch (crown y 51 m, outer 65.6 m)

details.description: X-lattice bracing on each leg with double diagonals and ~5 m chord pitch.
Stepped stone plinth courses: two pale steps with a thin dark seam each.
Bright catch-light line along each chord crest (worn chamfer gloss).
Deep shadow in the slots between lattice bars; darkest pixels #38322f.
Bright rivet crowns catching the key light: sub-centimetre specular dots.
Paint wear on leg outer corners and cornice edges exposing a lighter edge line.
Soft contact shadow under the plinths on the seamless paper; no horizon.
Paint a specular crescent on the dome glazing facing the key light.
Mid-shaft chord bands at ~5 m pitch with their own rivet rows.

preSpecAssessment.sourceImage: references/eiffel-hero.png (user-supplied reference image; not redistributed in this repository)

definitionOfDone: All 10 macro, 26 meso and 7 micro components exist as named nodes with the canonical CONTRACT.md ids.
The front-elevation render matches the measured silhouette profile within 5% of half-width at every 2% height sample and lands the three platform bands at their measured heights.
Lattice members, chords and rivets are real geometry/instancing; the frame reads hollow from the front and from +/-35 degree orbit views.
Five materials render with independent PBR channels; cavity darks come from AO + recess geometry, never from a dark albedo.
Reference-PBR extraction evidence at >= 0.7 confidence is wired for every render material and the reference-match framing reproduces ~94% frame height with a near-white backdrop.
Attachment contracts exist for every attached part and no part visibly floats.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette, taper and platform stack
qualityCriteria: Silhouette half-width must follow the measured profile: 79 m at y=15, 45.8 m at y=66, 37.0 m at y=87.8, 20.0 m at y=138.2, 17.8 m at y=151.2, 5.2 m at y=289, 8.9 m at y=289-300.6.
Three platform bands must sit at y 66-87.8, 138.2-151.2 and 289-300.6 m with correct width steps.
Base span (178.8 m over plinths) and total height (330 m) must match the measured aspect.
failureModes: tower reads as a straight cylinder or a 2D silhouette
platform bands land at wrong heights or all read the same width
leg splay is missing so the base looks like a column

featureGroups.name: Four legs, three platforms, two shafts, cupola and antenna
qualityCriteria: Every macro component exists as its own named node; no macro mass is merged into another.
Legs land on their own plinths and carry X-lattice bracing; shafts carry 4 corner posts + lattice.
Cupola and antenna sit on the platform-3 disc with their own pivots, not fused into the shaft.
failureModes: one fused mesh wearing the silhouette
legs/shafts built as solid plates instead of frames
cupola merged into the shaft so it cannot be exploded or re-posed

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every child part has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, gapTolerance.
Adjacent separate-geometry parts overlap at least 0.02 m at shared seams.
Tube-network members terminate on real chord joints, never float.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
lattice brace ends miss the chord ring
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Painted-iron surface response and recess shading
qualityCriteria: Five materials: ivory painted iron, shadowed crevice, worn edge highlight, cupola glass, studio backdrop.
Each render material has independent albedo/roughness/height/normal/AO and macro/meso/micro bands.
Shadows are produced by recess geometry + AO, not by a dark albedo.
failureModes: flat pale plastic look
dark paint faked with albedo instead of occlusion
albedo reused as roughness/height/AO

featureGroups.name: Reference colour, PBR extraction and studio lighting
qualityCriteria: Each render material carries usable referencePbr maps at confidence >= 0.7 (measured 0.846-0.86).
Key light soft neutral upper front-left, fill from camera-right, environment for pale-metal sheen.
Backdrop ~#f4f4f2, contact shadow only under the plinths, no dark horizon, ACES tone mapping.
failureModes: warm/grey photo tint instead of the pale studio palette
flat ambient-only lighting with no cavity separation
dark floor or visible cast horizon

featureGroups.name: Lattice rhythm and repeated systems
qualityCriteria: 26 chord rows over the upper shaft at 5.2 m pitch, 10 rows over the mid shaft at ~5 m pitch.
Double-diagonal X panels on all four faces; panels stay aligned across the platform steps.
Rivet rows ride the chords (instanced, not separate meshes).
failureModes: lattice appears as a texture decal rather than members
panel scale drifts between rows or faces
evenly spaced toy-like repetitive detail

featureGroups.name: Base arch crown and platform-1 frieze ornament
qualityCriteria: Segmental arch band with 4 concentric ribs, crown at y~51 m, outer crown ~65.6 m.
Rosette medallions along the intrados; X-lattice spandrel up to the platform-1 underside.
Platform-1 frieze arcade row and console brackets read at full-height framing.
failureModes: arch reads as a plain hole with no ornament
frieze band flattened into a plain box
arch crown too low/high versus the measured 51 m

featureGroups.name: Cupola, lantern and antenna apex
qualityCriteria: Ribbed dome + glazed drum + balustrade at y 298-312 m with a clean step over platform 3.
Antenna mast with stacked rings and a 12-point star finial at 330 m.
Apex silhouette holds at 94% frame height in the reference framing.
failureModes: apex is a plain cone
star finial missing so the silhouette loses its last 2 m
cupola reads wider than platform 3

visualDeltaChecks: silhouette and negative-space delta at 2% height samples
platform band height and half-width delta
material albedo/roughness/normal response delta (neutral + grazing + reference-match)
local ornament placement and scale delta (arch rosettes, frieze arcade, cupola ribs)
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if lattice, chords or rivets are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity look-dev from the source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap.
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners or lattice structure with a map alone when the feature affects form or silhouette.
mustNotDo: Do not darken the paint albedo to fake lattice shadow - use recess geometry + AO.
Do not collapse the four legs, three platforms or cupola into one mesh.
Do not fake the X lattice with a texture decal; rungs and chords must be members.
Do not replace the pale studio backdrop with a grey or dark environment.
Do not claim exact PBR recovery from the single reference image.

mustMatch: macro silhouette and the three platform steps
pale painted-iron albedo plus AO-driven cavity darks
lattice / chord / rivet rhythm at the measured pitches
arch crown band and platform-1 frieze ornament
reference PBR material response at >= 0.7 confidence
niceToHave: paint wear and handling scratches at leg corners
subtle sunward paint fade on the upper shaft front face
cupola glazing specular crescent matching the key light

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the pass 0-1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Review the identity-defining subsystems only: silhouette, platform stack, legs+arch, lattice rhythm, cupola+antenna, material system. Group repeated parts rather than reviewing each mesh.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: remaining gaps require new reference views

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs the reference image, the render screenshot, a side-by-side sheet, AI vision score, layer scores and critique before continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet; code pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Platform band heights and width steps
Legs, shafts, platforms and apex as separable structure
Leg splay and base arch profile
Pale painted-iron material system and recess shading
Cupola dome, glazing and antenna finial

sculptPipeline.blockedReason: blockout requires a browser screenshot and self-correction review before structural-pass unlocks
nextRequiredEvidence: AI vision score >= 0.7 with layer scores and mismatch critique
critical semantic feature scores from the same image pair meeting their thresholds
reviewHistory entry for blockout with action=continue

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: local colour/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local colour zones against the reference crop palette.
Compare roughness/normal/bump response under key light and grazing light.
Compare cavity dirt, paint wear and rivet catch-lights.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, backdrop and contact shadow.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness and tiling.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component is a stable named pivot with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for appended members, feet, decks, railings and ornament
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached members, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build from localStart to localEnd.
Represent detachable and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies instead of visual-mesh colliders.

destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups plus a small number of procedural fragments.

assumptions: Depth/lateral spacing is inferred from the 4-fold rotational symmetry of the tower: the reference is a single front elevation, so rear-leg placement, plinth depth and arch repetition on the far face are symmetry inferences, not direct observations.
The reference is a scale model, not the Paris tower: measured proportions (base span 178.8 m, platform 2 at 41.9% height) are used as-is rather than real-world Eiffel dimensions.
World total height is fixed at 330 m by CONTRACT.md; pixel measurements (1364 px tower height) set the 0.2419 m/px scale for every other dimension.

The single view cannot separate paint albedo from occlusion shading; the pale albedo and the dark lattice slots are modeled as albedo + AO/recess materials, and referencePbr is treated as evidence, not ground truth.
Contact shadow/backdrop is a scene-lighting fact recorded in lightingFromPhoto; it is not part of the exported asset geometry.

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: total height 330 m (CONTRACT.md); measured 0.2419 m/px on the 1364 px reference tower
coordinateFrame.note: Child transform.position, attachment.localStart/localEnd and socket localPosition are parent-pivot-relative; the root pivot sits at tower centre (0,165,0).

silhouette.boundingShape: Tapered four-legged lattice pylon on a four-pier plinth base; three platform bands (y 66-87.8, 138.2-151.2, 289-300.6 m); ribbed cupola and thin antenna crown it.
silhouette.symmetry: 4-fold rotational about Y; front/rear and left/right elevations are mirrored (depth inferred).
dominantCurves: straight leg splay 81.25 m -> 47.6 m outer half-width from y=15 to y=66 m (measured linear)
concave upper-shaft taper measured 17.9 -> 11.4 -> 7.7 -> 5.6 m half-width (a cone would be 1.9 m wider at mid-height)
segmental arch band between the legs (measured soffit R=41.4 m, crown 49.6 m)
ogee cupola dome over a glazed drum and gallery balcony
negativeSpaces: central arch opening: soffit circle R=41.4 m centred at y=8.2 m, crown 49.6 m (fit RMS 0.95 px)

base opening between the plinths: ~102-107 m clear at ground (measurer 444 px at y=1394 px = 106.9 m; independent row check 423 px = 101.8 m; a first measurer pass reported 569 px, so this value carries a +-2% measurement risk)
open lattice bays reading background through the frame
gaps between chord rows in both shafts

observations: Single object, centered (symmetry axis x=542.5 px), near-white studio backdrop #f0f1f2.
Tower spans y=28..1392 px (1364 px) = 330 m at 0.2419 m/px.
Three platform bands (y=1035..1140, 765..830, 160..197 px), cupola y=102..160, antenna y=28..102.
Foreground mask (lum < bg-22) covers 11.7% of the frame; bbox 1364 px tall, plinth span 739 px.
Four splayed lattice piers land on stepped stone pedestals; X-lattice on all visible faces.
Segmental decorative arch between the piers: crown at y~1190 px (51 m), 4 concentric ribs,
rosette medallions along the arch band, X-lattice spandrel up to the platform-1 underside.
Plinth steps read as two pale stone courses with a thin dark seam; soft contact shadow only.
Leg outer silhouette is straight with a slight inward lean; section narrows with height.
X-bracing with double-diagonal panels, horizontal chord every ~21 px (~5 m); rivet rows on chords.
Bright chord crests against dark bay slots give the leg its lattice read.
Platform-1 band: console brackets (arcade) y66-74 m, frieze panels 74-80 m,
deck/railing 80-87.8 m; outer half-width 45.8 m measured 188 px at y=1074 px.
Railing baluster rhythm and the frieze arcade row are the identity marks at this scale.
Mid shaft: four corner posts + X lattice, horizontal chords at ~5 m pitch.
Half-width tapers 37.0 m at y=87.8 m to 20.0 m at y=138.2 m (measured 86->152 px).
Slots between braces are dark; chord crests catch the key light.
Platform-2 deck at y=138.2..151.2 m, half-width 23.6 m (measured 98 px at y=791 px).
Frieze with modillion rhythm under the deck, railing on top; silhouette step is crisp.
Upper shaft: X-lattice panels, horizontal chord rings at 5.2 m pitch, 26 rows.
Half-width tapers 17.8 m at y=151.2 m to 5.2 m at y=289 m (measured 27->74 px at 0.4459 width ratio).
Vertical outer edges converge: fitted left/right slopes -0.0663/+0.0663 px/px.
Platform-3 disc + railing y=289..300.6 m (half 8.9 m); cupola/lantern y=298..312 m (half 3.9 m).
Cupola: glazed drum with arched mullions under a ribbed dome; 12 radial ribs on the dome.
Balcony rail around the drum base; the dome reads slightly brighter than the shaft.
Antenna spire y=312..330 m: thin mast with a stack of small rings/crossarms at 309..317 m.
A 12-point star finial crowns the mast at 328..330 m (span ~16 px = 3.9 m).
Mast is the only element thin enough to read against the backdrop at full tower height.
Platform-1 frieze band crop: dense ornament, deep dark slots between members.
Pixel percentiles 1% #38322f / 5% #504d48; extracted confidence 0.846 (target 0.7).
The darks are occlusion/recess shading of the same pale paint, not a second albedo.
Upper-shaft lattice crop: chord crests catch a bright rim (#E0DED9 at 90%) over #595450 slots.
Extracted confidence 0.86; palette #E0DED9/#827D78/#A7A29C/#C7C3BE/#595450.
Reads as worn/chamfered edge gloss on painted iron, not a polished specular surface.
Cupola crop: glazing reads as pale grey-green translucent panes with dark mullions.
Extracted confidence 0.86; palette #CCCAC6/#B6B3AF/#DFDEDB/#938E8A/#4F4B46.
No caustics or refraction cues visible at this scale - glass stays a thin transmission layer.
Seamless studio paper: border median #f0f1f2, luminance 241.9/255, noise sigma ~1.4.
Contact shadow under the plinths only (soft, no dark horizon, no cast shadow on backdrop).

componentTree.name: Eiffel Tower (root container)
componentTree.topologyRationale: The model is a 7,300 t puddled-iron frame assembled from 18,038 rolled members, not a carved or cast shell: every visible surface in the reference is a member edge or a joint, so the whole object is classified as an assembled solid.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: container node for the whole tower; bounds are the full 178.8 x 330 x 178.8 m box, no rendered mass of its own

collider.notes: axis-aligned proxy; the factory may refine per-part collider shapes

surfaceDetail.notes: Root is a pivot/metadata node; material assigned only so the runtime node is renderable if a proxy is ever needed.

componentTree.name: Stepped stone plinths (four piers)
componentTree.topologyRationale: Four stepped masonry pedestals are visible at the foot of the legs: two pale stone courses with a thin dark setback seam, each carrying an iron foot casting. They are separate built masses, not a continuous foundation slab.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: four stepped pedestals: lower course 42 x 3 x 42 m at y 0-3, upper course 40 x 4 x 40 m at y 3-7, cap course 38 x 8 x 38 m at y 7-15, centred on +/-68.4 m in X and Z

collider.notes: axis-aligned proxy; the factory may refine per-part collider shapes

localFeatures.name: Plinth step courses
localFeatures.geometryEffect: two recessed stepped courses with 0.35 m setback seams
localFeatures.materialEffect: seam AO darkening on each setback + bright step nosing

surfaceDetail.edgeWearPattern: step nosing catches a pale line
surfaceDetail.notes: Pale stone reads slightly matte/rougher than the iron above it.

hiddenRegions: rear pedestal pair hidden behind the front pair

componentTree.name: Four splayed lattice legs
componentTree.topologyRationale: The reference shows four separate lattice piers splaying out from the platform-1 underside to the plinths, each with X-bracing on its faces; they are distinct assembled trusses, not a solid base body.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: bounding box of the four piers: outer silhouette half-width 81.25 m at y=15 tapering linearly to 47.6 m at y=66; each pier section 26 m at the foot tapering to 15 m at the top; pier centres +/-68.25 m at the foot moving to +/-40.1 m at the top

collider.notes: axis-aligned proxy; the factory may refine per-part collider shapes

hiddenRegions: rear leg pair occluded by the front legs

componentTree.name: Decorative base arches (four faces)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A segmental decorative arch band spans between each pair of legs on all four faces: four concentric ribs with rosette medallions and an X-lattice spandrel. It is built from separate curved members, so it is an assembled solid rather than a cut opening in a wall.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: segmental arc band per face: measured soffit circle fits across two measurer passes give centre y=8.2-10.3 m, R=39.9-41.4 m, crown 49.3-50.2 m (RMS 0.95-4.0 px); four concentric ribs spaced 3.6 m with an outer rib crown ~56.8 m; spandrel lattice fills from the outer rib up to the platform-1 underside at y=66 m. Lead's authored construction values (inner arc centre (0,13.6) R=37.4, outer R=52) are noted as a 1.4-1.7 m crown deviation in authoring-notes.md; the spec adopts the measured crown 49.6 m.

collider.notes: axis-aligned proxy; the factory may refine per-part collider shapes

surfaceDetail.notes: Arch band is the strongest ornamental read in the lower third.

hiddenRegions: intrados partly hidden by the legs

materials.name: Ivory painted iron (primary structural paint)

albedo.samplingNotes: Reference-derived palette from the mid-shaft lattice crop; de-lit so baked key-light emphasis is not authored as albedo. Darkest sampled 5% (#504D48) belongs to occlusion, not to this albedo.

colorVariation.pattern: reference-derived mottling with cavity darkening and chord-crest brightening

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: Hold a stable ~1 m texel pitch across the 330 m tower; because lattice members are sub-metre, triplanar projection is used so micro paint grain does not stretch on long chord tubes.

surfaceFrequencyBands.role: broad painted-iron value breakup along the full tower height
lattice bay scale: chord bands, X-brace shading and joint shadowing
paint-film orange peel and rivet-dome highlight breakup under grazing light

roughness.localResponse: rougher inside lattice bays and joints, smoother on chord crests and worn edges; the measured reference roughness estimate (0.62) and the extracted roughness map (median 0.779, inflated by baked occlusion) are evidence, never albedo.

metalness.localResponse: painted dielectric over iron; the measured reference metalness estimate is 0.05, so the paint dominates and metalness rises only where paint is worn on chord crests.

bump.pattern: paint-film orange peel plus rivet domes

displacement.pattern: none at macro; chord relief is carried by real geometry

ambientOcclusion.notes: AO darkens lattice slot floors, member intersections and platform undersides; it must stay coherent with the shadowed-crevice material that fills the deepest bays.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then instance/merge repeated members without removing silhouette-visible lattice.

materials.ivory-painted-iron: pale warm-grey painted iron - primary structural paint over the whole lattice (albedo #D8D3C8, dominant #DFDDD8, roughness 0.64, metalness 0.08, 2048 px maps)
materials.iron-shadowed-crevice: recess/backing shade for lattice bays, arch intrados and platform undersides - the same pale paint under deep occlusion (AO cavity 0.85, darkest measured #2E2A26)
materials.iron-edge-highlight: worn chamfer and rivet-crown gloss on chord crests, rivet heads, balusters, star finial and arch rosettes (albedo #E9E5DA, roughness 0.30, clearcoat 0.35)
materials.cupola-glass: pale grey-green cupola glazing (albedo #C9D2D2, transmission 0.82, ior 1.5, roughness 0.14, clearcoat)
materials.studio-backdrop: seamless studio paper backdrop #F4F4F2 (utility tier) with a soft contact shadow under the plinths only, no dark horizon

reviewManifestHints.referenceCameraStatus: unsolved - verify reference-match framing by overlay
reviewManifestHints.note: Use these flags in the review manifest: approximate components are not to be scored as observed geometry; hidden regions are 4-fold/mirror symmetry inferences from a single front elevation.

lightingFromPhoto: key light: soft neutral diffused key from upper front-left (~5600K, ~35 deg elevation, ~20 deg left of camera), intensity 2.2, shadow radius 4-6 with a tight shadow-camera frustum; no hard dark shadow line on the backdrop.
fill light: broad neutral 5600K fill from camera-right at ~0.6 the key intensity to open lattice slots without flattening the cavity darks.
rim/environment light: neutral studio environment (RoomEnvironment-equivalent) at ~0.35 intensity so pale painted-metal chord crests and the cupola glazing separate from the near-white backdrop.
exposure and tone mapping: ACESFilmicToneMapping, exposure 1.05, outputColorSpace sRGB; target backdrop luminance ~0.95 in the rendered frame.
background: seamless studio paper #f4f4f2 with a very slight top-to-bottom gradient; no visible floor line.

contact shadow: soft ShadowMaterial-style contact shadow under the plinths only (opacity ~0.16, blurred), grounding the model without a dark horizon; ambient occlusion from recess geometry handles the lattice darks.
proceduralStrategy: Block out macro silhouette from the measured half-width profile before any detail.

Build the structure as a tube network: every leg, post, chord and brace is a member between measured endpoints (attachment.localStart/localEnd + baseRadius), because a single curve-sweep smooths a frame into a teardrop.
Emit the X-lattice and rivet rows as InstancedMesh repetition systems, never as one component per rung.
Keep four platform pivots, the cupola pivot and the antenna pivot separate so the tower can be exploded and re-posed without rebuilding geometry.
Run reference PBR extraction per material crop and keep the extracted maps as evidence for roughness/normal/AO response; never project the reference photo as albedo.
Carry silhouette-visible relief (arch ribs, frieze arcade, brackets, railing) as real geometry; reserve maps for paint-scale response.
Match the reference studio lighting only after materials read correctly under neutral turntable light.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale and visibility
base-legs, shaft-mid, shaft-upper, platform-1..3, lantern-cupola and antenna-spire expose stable named pivots for dissection/explode, with sockets at each attachment
leg-se/sw/ne/nw pivots sit at their foot sockets so a leg can be detached without rebuilding the base
antenna-spire and finial-star pivots allow tip swing or removal
destructionAnchors: destructionGroups: base-assembly (plinths+legs+arches), platform-stack (platforms 1-3), shaft-assembly, cupola-assembly, antenna-assembly
break seams follow real construction joints: plinth top, platform underside, platform-3 disc, cupola sill
lattice bays are the natural fragment scale for shaft damage; chords and posts stay with their host group
